findings.title: csv_rows joins values without calling csv_escape
findings.body:
`csv_rows` builds each line with a bare `",".join(...)` over stringified cell values, so any value containing a comma or a double quote silently corrupts the output (an extra column appears, and downstream parsers mis-align every field after it). The `csv_escape` helper added ten lines below in the same file is exactly the fix but is never invoked. Change the comprehension to `",".join(csv_escape(str(r.get(c, ""))) for c in columns)`.

_Also raised by the security agent:_ csv_rows joins values unescaped, bypassing csv_escape

findings.title: csv_escape assumes str input and ignores embedded newlines
findings.body: Two boundary cases are missed. (1) `"," in value` raises `TypeError: argument of type 'int' is not iterable` for any non-string cell, which is the common case for numeric report columns — either coerce with `str(value)` first or document the str-only contract. (2) A value containing `\n` or `\r` needs quoting too under RFC 4180, but falls through to the unquoted return on line 14 and breaks the record into two rows. Extend the condition to cover newline characters.

findings.title: New exporter functions across three files are untested
findings.body: csv_rows, csv_escape, dump_streaming, dump_pretty, margins_for, and usable_width are all new public functions with no accompanying tests. If any had an off-by-one (e.g. chunk_size boundary in dump_streaming), a wrong margin calculation in margins_for, or an escaping bug in csv_escape (e.g. values containing newlines), nothing in the suite would catch it. The repo already has a precedent (test_csv_header_matches_columns) for testing these small pure functions directly on their output, so at least a couple of representative tests (e.g. csv_escape with a comma/quote value, and dump_streaming chunk boundaries) would meaningfully raise confidence.

findings.title: csv_rows does not use csv_escape, emitting malformed CSV
findings.body:
`csv_rows` joins raw stringified field values with commas and never routes them through `csv_escape`, which is defined immediately below in the same module for exactly this purpose. Any row value containing a comma or a double quote (e.g. `{"a": "Smith, John"}`) produces a line with an extra field and unbalanced quoting, which downstream CSV parsers will read as a different number of columns than `csv_header` declares. Wrap the value: `",".join(csv_escape(str(r.get(c, ""))) for c in columns)`.

_Also raised by the security agent:_ csv_rows does not use csv_escape, allowing field/row injection

findings.title: New exporter functions across three files ship with no tests
findings.body: csv_rows, csv_escape, dump_streaming, dump_pretty, margins_for, and usable_width are all new public functions with non-trivial logic (edge-case escaping, chunking arithmetic, margin math) and none are covered by any test in this diff. The existing repo convention (reports/tests/test_csv.py tests csv_header directly) suggests each exporter function is normally given a direct unit test. If any of these had an off-by-one (e.g. dump_streaming's chunk boundary), a swapped margin order in margins_for, or a broken escaping condition in csv_escape (e.g. missing case where value contains both comma and quote, or non-string values), nothing in the test suite would catch it.

findings.title: csv_rows never applies csv_escape, emitting malformed CSV
findings.body: `csv_rows` joins raw `str(...)` values with commas, so a field whose value contains a comma or a double quote injects extra columns or unbalanced quotes into the output line. `csv_escape`, added in the same commit and clearly intended for exactly this, is never called. Wrap each field: `",".join(csv_escape(str(r.get(c, ""))) for c in columns)`. Note that `csv_escape` also assumes a `str` argument (`"," in value` raises `TypeError` on an int), so escape after the `str()` conversion, not before.

findings.title: csv_rows joins values without using csv_escape
findings.body: `csv_rows` renders each field with `str(r.get(c, ""))` and joins on `,`, bypassing the `csv_escape` helper defined immediately below. Any field value containing a comma, a double quote, or a newline shifts or splits columns in the output, letting whoever controls a row value forge additional columns or rows in the exported report. Route each field through `csv_escape` (and extend `csv_escape` to also quote values containing `\r` or `\n`, which it currently passes through unquoted), or use the stdlib `csv` module which handles all three cases.

findings.title: New exporter functions (CSV, JSON, PDF) lack any tests
findings.body: This PR adds six new public functions (csv_rows, csv_escape, dump_streaming, dump_pretty, margins_for, usable_width) across three files, none of which are covered by tests. The repository already has a precedent of testing exporter functions (test_csv_header_matches_columns), so these new functions fall below the existing coverage standard. If csv_escape mishandled quoting, or dump_streaming produced overlapping/incorrect chunks, or margins_for computed wrong margins, nothing in the test suite would catch it. Recommend adding at least one test per function exercising its core behavior (e.g. escaping a value with both comma and quote, streaming rows across a chunk boundary, and margin arithmetic for a known page size).
